Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Please don't change its password, profile details, or notification settings. You can place a reservation on the title River Glass, but don't cancel either of the two existing holds. If the app asks for a pickup branch, choose East Market, and note whether the selected branch is announced after the choice. The title is in the catalog on both platforms, but availability can change during the week, so record what the app shows at the time rather than treating a copy count as fixed.

Please also check whether headings are exposed as headings and whether repeated controls have enough context to distinguish them. In the holds list, there are two buttons labeled “More.” One is for the hold on River Glass and the other is for A Map of Salt. We need to know whether the screen reader announces which hold each button belongs to, not just the word “More.”

For the search task, search for River Glass by title and do not use voice input. Record whether the query can be edited, whether the clear-search control is announced, and whether the result count is spoken when the results load. On the title details screen, check the author, format, availability message, and reservation control. If the reservation control is unavailable because all copies are checked out, do not try to bypass it; record the announced reason and continue with the holds-list checks. If it is available, place the reservation at East Market and check the confirmation message and the updated holds list. In either case, do not remove or edit an existing hold.

Please organize the findings in these sections:
1. Test setup and versions, including the date and time of each session.
2. Task steps and the result on each platform.
3. Screen-reader announcement or focus problems, with the exact screen and control named.
4. Any differences between iOS and Android that affect completing the tasks.
5. Open questions that need a product or library answer.

For an issue, describe the steps needed to encounter it, what VoiceOver or TalkBack announced, and what you expected it to announce. Keep the expected behavior tied to the task, rather than recommending a specific implementation. If a problem happens only after repeating an action, say how many times you repeated it and whether it happened on both platforms. Please don't call a problem intermittent just because it was seen once. If you can't reproduce something, state that plainly and include the path you tried. We also need the app version, operating system, screen reader, and test time next to each finding so that engineering can repeat the same setup.

Mara from the library team said, “The labels are still being reviewed, so please tell us what the reader actually says before suggesting replacement wording.” Please include exact spoken labels when they are relevant, but don't infer a label from the visible text if the screen reader says something different. The team is comparing the audit with a list of known issues, so note whether each finding is new to this session or matches an item already on that list. The list is in the shared Northline folder under Accessibility / Current Issues, and the version there is dated May 6. If you cannot open that folder, leave the match status unconfirmed rather than guessing.

If build 4.8.2 is available in TestFlight by Thursday at noon, repeat the search and reservation checks on that build and label those results separately from the 4.8.1 results; otherwise, complete the requested work on 4.8.1 and state that 4.8.2 was not available by that time. If it occurs only on 4.8.2, identify that condition and don't describe it as a public-release problem.
